summary: Texas Forest Service steel lookout in southeastern Anderson County, built 1928 at about 90 ft; a 1946 fire report names its patrolman; FFLA lists it gone.

facts.design: Standard-type steel lookout: square cab on a four-legged trussed tower, painted grey
facts.status_note: FFLA list marks it gone; the sources read give no removal date or account of how it came down

events.note: Texas Forest Service, with Southern Pine Lumber Company and Houston County Timber Company, erected two 90-foot steel towers in 1928; the other stood at Ratcliff, Houston County
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description calls it about 90 feet high, painted grey, a standard steel lookout tower
Report dated August 15, 1946 names Forest Patrolman L.P. Johnson of the Bird Mountain tower; one forest fire, one acre burned over

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The Alto Herald report says western Houston County and The Forest Worker report says eastern Houston County. The story states the disagreement; the Bird Mountain facts do not depend on it.

notes_for_editor: The 1928 build and the 90-foot height are supported by two 1928 newspaper reports, both quoted on the Forest Lookouts page rather than read in their original papers. Those reports disagree on the Ratcliff companion tower (western or eastern Houston County). The 27.140 m / 89.04 ft figure in the 1942 NGS description is the distance from triangulation station BIRD to the tower point, not the tower height. Height 27.4 m matches the 'about 90 feet' in the sources. No removal date or account of the site's fate was found beyond the FFLA gone status, and no site-condition source was found. The 1946 report names a patrolman 'of the Bird Mountain tower' but says nothing about staffing levels, so no staffing fact is recorded.
